external_entities.name: developer
external_entities.description: Writes changes and pushes branches to the self-hosted git server; can also log in to the build runner and trigger an unreviewed rebuild of main by hand.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Developers push their branches to our self-hosted git server, which sits on the corporate network.

external_entities.name: public package registry
external_entities.description: Public dependency source on the internet that the build runner resolves the lockfile against.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Dependency resolution reaches out to the public package registry on the internet

processes.name: build runner
processes.description: Picks up a merge to main, fetches the source, resolves the dependency lockfile and produces a container image tagged with the commit sha. Holds the shared build token used to call the deploy controller.
processes.source_excerpt: The build runner picks the merge up, fetches the source, resolves the dependency lockfile and produces a container image.

processes.name: deploy controller
processes.description: Holds one record — which image sha the estate should be on. Set by the build runner, polled by every store server.
processes.source_excerpt: The deploy controller runs on the corporate network and holds one record: which image sha the estate should be on.

processes.name: store server
processes.description: The back-office server in each of about 1,200 stores, running the till software as a container. Polls the deploy controller once a minute and pulls and restarts on a new release.
processes.source_excerpt: Each store has a small server in the back office running the till software as a container.
processes.notes: One element stands for the whole fleet of ~1,200 identical servers; the source describes them collectively and states no per-store difference.
processes.technology: container runtime running the till software

data_stores.name: git server
data_stores.description: Self-hosted git server holding developer branches and main; a merge to main is what starts a build.
data_stores.source_excerpt: Developers push their branches to our self-hosted git server, which sits on the corporate network.
data_stores.notes: The source treats the git server both as somewhere source rests and as something developers push to; modelled as a Data Store, which is where the source code actually lives.

data_stores.name: image registry
data_stores.description: Holds the container images, tagged with the commit sha. Sits in the build environment and is reachable from the store estate over the WAN.
data_stores.source_excerpt: It pushes the finished image to our image registry, which is also in the build environment.

data_flows.name: push branches
data_flows.description: Developers push their branches to the git server; a merge to main is what starts a build.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Developers push their branches to our self-hosted git server, which sits on the corporate network.

data_flows.name: manual rebuild
data_flows.description: Any developer can log in to the build runner and kick off a rebuild of main by hand.
data_flows.source_excerpt: And any developer can log in to the build runner and kick off a rebuild of main by hand; that path does not require a merge and is not reviewed.
data_flows.data_description: an interactive login and a rebuild of main that any developer may trigger, requiring no merge and receiving no review

data_flows.name: fetch source
data_flows.description: The runner picks the merge up and fetches the source it is going to build.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The build runner picks the merge up, fetches the source, resolves the dependency lockfile and produces a container image.
data_flows.data_description: the source of the merged commit

data_flows.name: resolve dependencies
data_flows.description: The runner resolves the lockfile against the public package registry and takes what it downloads as given.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Dependency resolution reaches out to the public package registry on the internet, and the lockfile is taken as given — the runner does not verify signatures on what it downloads.
data_flows.authentication: none — the runner does not verify signatures on the packages it downloads
data_flows.data_description: dependency packages named by the lockfile, which is taken as given

data_flows.name: push image
data_flows.description: The runner pushes the finished image, tagged with the commit sha, to the registry.
data_flows.source_excerpt: It pushes the finished image to our image registry, which is also in the build environment.
data_flows.data_description: the built container image, tagged with the commit sha

data_flows.name: set current release
data_flows.description: The runner calls the controller and asks it to make the image it just pushed the current release.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The token the runner uses to call the controller is a shared build token that is the same for every pipeline and has not been rotated since the pipeline was set up.
data_flows.authentication: a shared build token, the same for every pipeline, never rotated since the pipeline was set up
data_flows.data_description: the image sha that should become the current release

data_flows.name: poll current release
data_flows.description: Every store server asks the controller once a minute what the current release is; the store initiates, nothing is pushed to it.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The store servers do not get pushed to. Every store server asks the deploy controller once a minute what the current release is
data_flows.data_description: the image sha the estate should be on

data_flows.name: pull image
data_flows.description: On a changed release the store server pulls that image from the registry over the WAN and restarts the container.
data_flows.source_excerpt: if it differs from what it is running it pulls that image from the registry and restarts the container. The registry allows the pull; nobody has written down what a store server presents to it
data_flows.data_description: the container image for the current release

trust_boundaries.name: corporate network
trust_boundaries.description: Holds the git server and the deploy controller, and is where developers sit.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: our self-hosted git server, which sits on the corporate network

trust_boundaries.name: build environment
trust_boundaries.description: The runner's own environment, stated to be separate from the corporate network; the image registry is in it too.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: The runner lives in its own build environment, separate from the corporate network.

trust_boundaries.name: store estate
trust_boundaries.description: About 1,200 back-office store servers, reaching the corporate network and the registry over the retail WAN.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: Traffic between the stores and the corporate network goes over the retail WAN.

trust_boundaries.name: internet
trust_boundaries.description: Where the public package registry sits.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: Dependency resolution reaches out to the public package registry on the internet

assumptions.assumption: Developers sit on the corporate network.
assumptions.basis: The git server they push to is stated to sit on the corporate network; the source places developers nowhere else.

assumptions.assumption: The build runner is not reachable from the internet.
assumptions.basis: Stated to live in its own build environment; the only internet interaction stated is outbound dependency resolution.

assumptions.assumption: The deploy controller is not reachable from the internet.
assumptions.basis: Stated to run on the corporate network and to be reached by store servers over the retail WAN.

assumptions.assumption: The store servers are not reachable from the internet.
assumptions.basis: Back-office servers reached over the retail WAN; the source states they do not get pushed to at all.
